walkthroughs.body_html:
Operations, Finance and Influences on Business — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Operations, Finance and Influences on Business brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Operations, Finance and Influences on Business.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Strategic
Specific
Strong
Saleable

mcqs.q: Which 1970 essay argued the 'social responsibility of business is to increase profits'?
options: Drucker
Porter
Friedman
Carroll

mcqs.q: When can a laissez-faire leadership style be effective?
options: Laissez-faire leadership means the leader doesn't care about the business.
Laissez-faire leadership is illegal under employment law.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
When employees are highly skilled, self-motivated and need autonomy — common in creative or expert teams. It can fail with inexperienced staff or in crises requiring direction.

mcqs.q: What are Porter's two main generic strategies for competitive advantage?
options: Laissez-faire leadership is illegal under employment law.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Porter says businesses should pursue both low cost and differentiation at once.
Cost leadership (being the lowest-cost producer) and differentiation (offering unique value customers will pay more for) — Porter argues firms should choose one or the other.
Porter's strategies are about marketing channels.
Holding minimal stock and receiving inputs only when needed for production — reducing storage costs but increasing vulnerability to supply disruption.
Just-in-time means delivering products to customers exactly on time.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.
